description:
From the fz-kdt.119 cold review (2026-09-01, at b32d645ac). The
callable demand for enum_take_drop_split's step carries two
resolutions -- (int, {empty_list(), int}) and (int, {list(int), int})
-- the accumulator specialized on both its INITIAL {[], 0} and its
grown form. Base's arity-only tuple test cannot separate them, so one
member takes every value (FZ_DEBUG_TUPLE_SHAPE: 54 occurrences of
{cons,int} passing a {[],int} test in this one fixture) and the other
is DEAD -- and BROKEN: its return form is shape{lane,lane} where its
sibling's is a packed lane({:cont|:halt, list(int)}); reached (by
making the test exact), the caller mis-marshals and a tuple arrives
where a list is expected ('backend callable construction 27 matched
no member'). The corpus contains dead specializations that are not
correctly built, kept harmless only by the blindness fz-kdt.119
removes. FZ_STRESS_REVERSE_DISPATCH_ARMS does NOT catch it (reversal
does not perturb construction-wrapper selection -- see the instrument
ticket). BLOCKS fz-kdt.119 Scope B (nested list positions). Fix
direction: either the initial-form specialization should not be
minted separately (it is subsumed by the grown form -- cross-key
subsumption smell, fz-kdt.124's neighborhood) or its return contract
must agree with its siblings (fz-kdt.97's one-return-contract law for
construction members).

comments.text:
CONFIRMED and QUANTIFIED from fz-kdt.119's landing (4ca1dc7e7), which shipped the carve-out this ticket blocks.

The carve-out is one function, read by the lattice and by all three lowerings alike: runtime_type_predicate::lowering_tests_position -- a tuple position whose sub-predicate can admit a LIST is not tested at all. Testing only its non-list axes would make the test STRICTER than the type (a position's question is a disjunction; dropping a disjunct rejects values the arm's surface names), so the choice was to decide the list axis there or be blind, and deciding it is what reaches this ticket's dead-and-broken member. Blind counts as overlapping AND as erasing, so no seat can claim it as separation.

The new tripwire measures the cost of staying blind. FZ_STRESS_ASSERT_SURFACE_MEMBERSHIP=1 over the corpus at head reports 106 escapes on 00420_enum_take_drop_split and 106 on behavior/enum_take_drop_split (the same program by two paths) -- 212 of the baseline's 268, and a sampled line shows exactly the shape this ticket names: lists {Empty} at position 0 of a 2-tuple, taking a cons.

So this ticket is the single largest entry in the tripwire baseline, and closing it is what lets fz-kdt.138 flip lowering_tests_position to true and take those 212 with it.

fz-kdt.141's wrapper-permutation stress: THE MEASURED VERDICT IS A NEGATIVE, honestly reported.

The wrapper half now exists (FZ_STRESS_PERMUTE_DISPATCH=wrappers:<seed> permutes flow.first_class_edges in jobs/runtime_demand.rs, upstream of members AND selection, so fz-kdt.108's body_id weld holds). It DOES reach this ticket's pair: the backend canon of enum_take_drop_split moves 972 lines under wrappers:1, and the moved lines are the selection plan's own test nodes swapping -- 'n2 test s1 type(fp[T] {list(int), int})' becomes 'n2 test s1 type(fp[T] {empty_list(), int})'. So the perturbation lands exactly on the {empty_list(), int} / {list(int), int} pair this ticket names.

IT DOES NOT PRODUCE 'backend callable construction 27 matched no member', on any door, at any seed. stdout and exit are identical across the whole 584-fixture corpus, interp and JIT, and across the census fixtures on AOT.

WHY, and it sharpens this ticket rather than weakening it: reordering does not make the dead member LIVE ALONGSIDE its sibling, it makes it live INSTEAD of it. The tuple test is blind at the list position, so whichever member is first takes every value -- one member is always dead. Each member is self-consistent when it takes everything (its own boundary marshals its own return form), so no caller ever sees two disagreeing return contracts. The break this ticket describes needs the two members reached by DIFFERENT values, which is exactly what fz-kdt.138's exact test does and what no ordering can do. So an order stress can never catch this class, and fz-kdt.136's expectation ('expected immediate catch: the take_drop blocker') is refuted by measurement.

WHAT THE WRAPPER STRESS DID CATCH is bigger and is filed as fz-kdt.147: the whole 268-escape FZ_STRESS_ASSERT_SURFACE_MEMBERSHIP baseline is wrapper-order-decided (268 settled -> 68 at wrappers:1 -> 20 at wrappers:6, five of seven fixtures to zero, this fixture 106 -> 34 -> 10), and arm-order seeds move it by ZERO. The settled order is the worst of the legal orders. This ticket owns the largest entry in that baseline, so 147 is its immediate neighbour.

title: P1: a dead-because-blind accumulator specialization does not work when reached
